questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how the worker threads pull and run jobs from the shared queue? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
What causes the worker threads to exit when the WorkerPool is dropped?
choices: The sender is dropped, so recv() returns Err once the queue is empty and the worker loop ends
The pool calls handle.abort() on every thread
The Arc around the receiver reaching zero strong references terminates the threads
Each worker checks a shutdown flag between jobs

questions.prompt: A job closure panics while running on a worker thread. What happens to the pool?
choices: The panic is converted into an Err returned from submit
Only that job is lost and the worker keeps serving the queue
The panicking worker thread terminates; the pool does not replace it, and the panic is reported when Drop joins it

questions.prompt: In main, why is the pool dropped explicitly before the final println of the routed count?
choices: The AtomicUsize is only valid until the pool is gone
It cancels jobs that have not started
Dropping releases memory so the count is accurate
Drop waits for all workers to finish queued jobs, so every increment has happened before the count is read
